current_example.title: Example: Calculating the Second Moment of a Random Variable

q-149701.name: Question 1
q-149701.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{3}{{x}^{4}},\,x\ge 1.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
q-149701.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }3{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{3}{x}|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =-(0-\frac{3}{1}) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

q-149701.html:
Question 1
?

A continuous random variable X has the probability density function

f(x)=3x4,x≥1.

Calculate E[X2].

a
2
b
13
c
23
d
32
e
3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a continuous random variable X with probability density function f(x) defined over a set S, the expected value of X2 is given by

E[X2]=∫Sx2⋅f(x)dx.

We compute the expected value of X2 as follows:

E[X2]=∫1∞x2⋅3x4dx=∫1∞3x2dx=∫1∞3x−2dx=−3x|1∞=−(0−31)=3

q-149702.name: Question 2
q-149702.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 1<x\le 2, \\ \frac{x}{5}, & 2\le x<3.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
q-149702.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{{x}^{3}}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\,{|}_{1}^{2}+{\frac{{x}^{4}}{20}|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =(2-1)+(\frac{81}{20}-\frac{16}{20}) \\  & =1+\frac{13}{4} \\  & =\frac{17}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

A continuous random variable X has the probability density function

f(x)={1x2,1<x≤2,x5,2≤x<3.

Calculate E[X2].

a
174
b
5
c
134
d
195
e
245

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a continuous random variable X with probability density function f(x) defined over a set S, the expected value of X2 is given by

E[X2]=∫Sx2⋅f(x)dx.

So, we compute the expected value of X2 as follows:

E[X2]=∫13x2⋅f(x)dx=∫12x2⋅1x2dx+∫23x2⋅x5dx=∫12dx+∫23x35dx=x|12+x420|23=(2−1)+(8120−1620)=1+134=174

q-152895.name: Question 3
q-152895.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{8}\,x,\,0\le x\le 4.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
q-152895.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{8}\,x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{32}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{32}(256-0) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

q-152897.name: Question 4
q-152897.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}x, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{3}\,x, & 1\le x<2.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
q-152897.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{12}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(1-0)+\frac{1}{12}(16-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{5}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-152898.name: Question 5
q-152898.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 1\le x<3.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
q-152898.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\,{x}^{5}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+x\,{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1-0)+(3-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+2 \\  & =\frac{11}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
